breaking_changes: Version format changed from X.Y.Z (e.g., 11.9.0) to YYYY.WW.N (e.g., 2026.39.0); any tool or script parsing the version string must be updated.

Model registry field registry_source now defaults to empty string instead of 'huggingface' in GET /pull/variants and GET /models responses; clients assuming a non-empty value may misinterpret the source.
The unversioned /docs endpoint now returns JSON 404 instead of falling through to the SPA web-app; any reliance on that fallback is removed.

evidence.blockers: The new candidate release pipeline (weekly branch creation, prerelease publishing, candidate Docker tag) has never been exercised end-to-end in production — a human must trigger the full path to confirm artifacts land correctly. The version format change replaces CMake static versioning with a Python-based dynamic system that adds a hard Python3 build dependency. The FLM ModelScope download path has only unit test coverage. The wildcard origin feature and image edit endpoint are new user-reachable surfaces without independent manual verification.
evidence.breaking_changes: The version format shift from semantic X.Y.Z to YYYY.WW.N is the most visible breaking change, affecting any consumer that parses --version output or build metadata. The registry_source empty-string default is a subtle API encoding change that affects all consumers of GET /models and GET /pull/variants for FLM models. The unversioned /docs JSON 404 replaces an undocumented SPA fallback — a deliberate fix rather than an unintended break, but it changes behavior for anyone who reached that path.
evidence.coverage: The range v11.9.0 to a1c8e7be covers 43 commits across the full release. CI passed on all checked commits, with automated coverage including C++ unit tests, server endpoint tests, distro packaging builds, validation workflows for llama.cpp/vLLM/sd-cpp, and CodeQL. The items marked for manual testing were not exercised end-to-end by a human before merge; they cover new features or behavior changes where CI unit tests alone did not demonstrate the complete user path.
evidence.manual_testing: New feature paths that need human verification: wildcard port and subdomain CORS matching against the live server, /pull/variants filter exercising both the new error path and the retained happy path, MCP lemonade_docs tool end-to-end with an MCP client, session header relay through a real cloud provider, prompt cache preservation on soft-idle transition with auto_evict enabled, /images/edit endpoint on ROCm hardware with real image data, version string format in the release binary, the full candidate release pipeline (branch creation → prerelease publish → Docker candidate tag → GitHub release page display).
evidence.security: No security issues observed. The wildcard origin feature was reviewed by a security-area maintainer with strict dot-boundary subdomain enforcement and documented security warnings for universal wildcards. The session header relay uses a strict well-known-only allowlist with cross-request isolation via thread-local storage and discovery endpoint exemption. The vendored model-viewer bundle pinning with SHA-256 drift guard reduces supply-chain risk. No credential handling changes, obfuscation, or suspicious code paths were introduced.
